Progressive joint stiffness over 8 months with significant functional impairment in daily activities

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 34-year-old female with hypothyroidism and history of alcohol use disorder in remission who returns for rheumatology follow-up regarding joint symptoms initially evaluated in January 2020. She reports that the stiffness is particularly pronounced in the morning and can last over an hour before it begins to ease with movement. The discomfort is most noticeable in her wrists, hands, and ankles. She describes difficulty gripping items, turning doorknobs, and typing at her job as a writer. She also mentions fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and a recent unintended weight loss of 3 kilograms over the last few months. She denies any trauma, rash, visual symptoms, or recent illnesses.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-07-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Patel, MD
Department: Internal Medicine
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Worsening symmetric joint pain over past 4 months with new knee involvement

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
A 33-year-old female with hypothyroidism and alcohol use disorder in remission returns for follow-up of progressive joint symptoms with new knee involvement over four months. She describes stiffness in the morning that lasts over an hour and gradually improves throughout the day. The discomfort began in her wrists and now affects the small joints of her hands and knees, all of which feel swollen and tender. The symptoms are symmetric. She denies any fevers, skin rashes, or prior trauma.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Rheumatoid arthritis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Hypothyroidism
- History of alcohol use disorder (in remission)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Tonsillectomy (age 8)
- Wisdom teeth extraction (age 21)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Levothyroxine 88 mcg PO daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
Her sister was recently diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: History of alcohol use disorder in remission for 2 years; currently drinks socially on occasion. Occupation: Professional writer and classical pianist.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On exam, there is synovial thickening and tenderness over the bilateral metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory testing shows an ESR of 65 mm/hr, hemoglobin of 10.4 g/dL, and positive anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody.

OTHER STUDIES:
Synovial fluid aspiration from her right knee reveals 35,000 WBCs/μL and no organisms or crystals.
